Cherry eye surgery for bulldogs

Cherry eye is a prolapse of the third eyelid gland, common in English bulldogs and French bulldogs. Surgery repositions the gland rather than removing it, because the gland produces a large share of the tear film and removing it leads to dry eye later in life.

The pocket technique buries the gland under the conjunctiva and holds it with absorbable suture. Recovery takes ten to fourteen days with a soft collar. Recurrence happens in roughly ten per cent of dogs and a second procedure is usually successful.

Bulldogs frequently present with cherry eye in both eyes within a year, so we discuss the second eye at the first consultation even when it looks normal.
